# Weekly seller payouts

> Every Monday a job creates one [`Payout`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L7) per shop with enough balance, moves the money in the ledger, and a second job sends it through Stripe Connect, reversing the ledger if Stripe definitely refuses.

_Part of [domain/payments](../../units/domain/payments.md)_

The weekly job `payouts.run-weekly` lives in [`PayoutJobs`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L33). It is scheduled with cron `0 6 * * 1` (Monday 06:00, Europe/Warsaw), and the schedule is registered on app start. It works out the Monday of the current week (or uses `periodStart` if you pass one). Then it sums each shop's ledger balance and keeps shops with at least 10.00 (`MIN_PAYOUT_MINOR`, 1000 minor units). For each such shop, one database transaction does three things. It inserts a [`Payout`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L7) row. It posts a `PAYOUT` journal that moves the money from the shop's account to `PAYOUT_CLEARING`. It enqueues a `payouts.send` job. The [`Payout`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L7) table has a unique key on shop and week, so a re-run does nothing for shops already handled. If the insert is skipped, nothing is posted or enqueued. See [how journals work](ledger-posting-model.md) and [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md). The `payouts.send` job loads the payout and exits unless it is still `PENDING`. It then asks the payout provider to transfer the money to the shop's Stripe account, using the payout id as the idempotency key. On success it marks the payout `PAID` and moves the money from `PAYOUT_CLEARING` to `PAYOUTS_SENT`. Network or 5xx errors are rethrown so the job retries safely. A definite refusal marks the payout `FAILED` and posts a `PAYOUT_REVERSAL` journal that returns the money to the shop's balance. One bad shop never blocks the others, because each shop has its own send job.

**Look at:** [`PayoutJobs` in payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L33) · [`PayoutProvider` in payout-provider.port.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout-provider.port.ts#L12) · [`Payout` in payout.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L4) · [`FinanceWorkerModule` in finance-worker.module.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/finance-worker.module.ts#L28)

## Pieces

- [Payout row with one-per-shop-per-week rule](payout-model.md): The [`Payout`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L7) model stores amount, currency, week start, status (`PENDING`, `PAID`, `FAILED`), Stripe reference and failure reason, with a unique key on shop and week start.
- [Payout journals in the ledger](ledger-posting-model.md): A payout moves money shop account → `PAYOUT_CLEARING` → `PAYOUTS_SENT`, or back to the shop on failure, using journal ids that retries cannot duplicate.
- Payout provider abstraction: [`PayoutProvider`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout-provider.port.ts#L12) is an abstract class with `transfer`; [`StripeConnectPayoutProvider`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout-provider.port.ts#L17) calls Stripe, and [`FakePayoutProvider`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout-provider.port.ts#L29) is a test double that can be told to fail.
- [Retry versus reverse on send failure](send-failure-handling.md): Errors that are not definite are rethrown so the job retries; errors marked `definite` or of type `StripeInvalidRequestError` fail the payout and reverse the journal.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | [`Payout`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L7) | One row per shop per week is inserted with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. It is later updated to `PAID` or `FAILED`. |
| database | [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) | The weekly job sums balances of accounts starting with `SHOP_` to find shops that can be paid. |
| database | `Shop (stripeAccountId)` | The send job reads the shop's Stripe account id as the transfer destination. |
| job | `payouts.run-weekly` | Cron `0 6 * * 1`, Europe/Warsaw, concurrency 1. Creates payouts and enqueues sends. |
| job | `payouts.send` | Enqueued per payout with idempotency key `payout-send:<payoutId>`, concurrency 20. Does the transfer. |
| external | `Stripe Connect transfer` | Money goes to the shop's account via `StripeService.transfer`, with the payout id as the idempotency key. |

## Also relies on

- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): Calls `LedgerService.post` for the payout, sent and reversal journals inside the same transactions as the status changes.

## Watch out

- The schedule runs in Europe/Warsaw time, but [`mondayOf`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L130) computes the week start in UTC.
- Shops with less than 10.00 in balance are skipped, and nothing is created for them that week.
- The money leaves the shop's ledger balance as soon as the [`Payout`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L7) row is created, before Stripe is called. It only comes back if the transfer definitely fails.
- A payout whose transfer succeeds but whose status update then fails could be retried. Stripe dedupes this through the payout id key, so no double transfer happens.
